subject: Observa DPA — redlines on international transfers & subprocessors
messages:
From: Michael Lee <michael.lee@observa-analytics.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: legal@observa-analytics.com
Date: 2026-07-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Observa DPA redlines (first pass)

Vanessa —

Thanks again for the quick intro call this morning. Attached are our first-pass redlines to Redwood's standard DPA. High level: our counsel flagged the international transfer language, the subprocessors list, and the audit/incident notification timelines. We made a few proposed edits that reflect our compliance posture in the EU and a requested SLA for notification of data breaches affecting personal data.

Key asks in this version:
- Confirm support for SCCs (we paneled the EU Commission clauses inline) or provide equivalent transfer mechanism.
- Limit Redwood subprocessors to those listed in the Annex and require 30 days' notice before adding new subprocessors.
- Clarify retention and logging windows (we propose 13 months for access logs).
- Add KMS key custody language — we need assurance that customer-managed keys are supported for this workload.

I've attached Observa_DPA_Redlines_v1.docx. Emily from Harrison & Co. is on copy and can pick up detailed negotiating points. Please let us know which items you can accept as-is and which you want to counter.

Best,
Michael
Head of Legal Operations
Observa Analytics

If there are items we can't accept, we'll propose alternative mitigations (e.g., annex-based subprocessors + 30-day notice with emergency exception).

Date: 2026-07-03T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observa DPA redlines (first pass) — counsel notes

Vanessa / Team —

I reviewed Observa's redlines and annotated the document (see attached Counsel_Annotated_DPA.pdf). High-level guidance below so we can be aligned before we send back counter language to Observa:

1) International transfers — SCCs vs. equivalent:
   - We can accept SCCs for EU transfers. Redwood will execute the standard EU SCCs with technical and organizational measures appended.
   - For UK data, we will propose the UK Addendum (or include equivalent clauses). If Observa insists on a specific mechanism, ask them to confirm their data flow map so we can scope any extra obligations.

2) Subprocessors & notice period:
   - 30 days' notice for new subprocessors is reasonable for commercial additions, but we need an emergency carve-out for security patches and urgent infra changes (48–72 hour notice with post-facto notification acceptable).
   - We should keep the Annex dynamic: Redwood will publish a current subprocessors list in the Console and provide email notice. Suggest language: "Redwood will notify Customer of additions to the Subprocessor list at least 30 days prior to engagement, except in emergency situations requiring faster onboarding."

3) Logging & retention windows:
   - We cannot commit to customer-defined retention for platform-level access logs beyond operational constraints. We can offer 13 months retention for security/audit logs as a commercial add-on or include a retention SLA for production logs. Recommend: offer 13 months as default for access logs and clarify scope.

4) KMS / Customer-managed keys:
   - Redwood supports customer-managed keys for encryption-at-rest in Private deployments. For Hosted (multi-tenant) currently we offer a bring-your-own-key option via our KMS integration for enterprise customers on Dedicated/Private tiers. We should be explicit about availability and any additional costs.

5) Breach notification SLA:
   - Observa's requested "immediate" notification is too vague. We should propose 72 hours for confirmed incidents affecting personal data, with interim notifications if investigation is ongoing. This aligns with standard incident response expectations.

6) Audits & third-party requests:
   - We can accept SOC2-type attestations and provide redacted reports. On-site audits are limited; we provide third-party audit reports and accommodate remote evidence review where possible.

Next steps: I'll draft counterlanguage for the SCC/UK addendum paragraph, the subprocessors clause with emergency carve-out, and the breach notification timeline. Vanessa / Priyom — if you have commercial constraints or deal points to weigh in on (credits, pilot window, timeline to signature), flag them now so I can fold them into the language.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Counsel_Annotated_DPA.pdf]

From: Emily Harrison <emily.harrison@harrisonlaw.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Michael Lee <michael.lee@observa-analytics.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-05T15:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observa DPA redlines (first pass) — Observa counterpoints

Neha / Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick review. Observa's counsel had two follow-ups after our call:

1) They are pushing for a narrower definition of "Emergency" in your subprocessor carve-out. They suggested: "Emergency means a security incident or critical patch required to maintain availability." Can Redwood accept that narrower trigger if we keep the 48–72 hour notice mechanism?

2) KMS: Observa reiterated they want proof of customer-managed key availability for Hosted customers (they said this is a hard requirement for the pilot). If Redwood cannot confirm availability in Hosted, they'd like to understand the migration path to Dedicated/Private and associated lead times/costs.

3) Logging retention: Observa wants a specific clause guaranteeing 13 months for access logs related to customer accounts. They indicated this is tied to their internal retention policy.

Observa is willing to proceed if we accept SCCs and the subprocessors timeline with the narrower emergency definition, plus a clear statement on the KMS roadmap. They asked if we can route the final DPA through DocuSign after the technical clarifications are agreed.

Please advise on the emergency wording and KMS/Hosted feasibility. Happy to jump on a short call if that speeds resolution.

Emily Harrison
Partner, Harrison & Co.

Subject: Re: Observa DPA — redlines on international transfers & subprocessors

Michael / Emily —

Thanks for the patience while we worked through counsel comments. Attached is Redwood's proposed counter (we updated the Annex language and included the SCCs + UK addendum text). Key points:

- Subprocessors: we accepted the 30-day notice and the emergency carve-out but will use the narrower emergency definition you proposed: "Emergency means a security incident or critical patch required to maintain availability."
- KMS: for the Hosted pilot we cannot support customer-managed keys at this time. We will include a clear migration path to Dedicated/Private (lead time typically 6–8 weeks) and offer a commercial credit during migration for pilot customers.
- Logging retention: we agreed to provide 13 months for access/security logs relating to Observa accounts as part of the pilot addendum.
- Breach notifications: Redwood will commit to interim notification within 24 hours of detection and a confirmed report within 72 hours of confirmation.

If everything above tracks, we'll prepare the final DPA and route via DocuSign. DocuSign link will be: https://docusign.example.com/OBSV-DPA-2026. Please confirm acceptance of the emergency definition and the Hosted KMS limitation (with migration path). Once confirmed, we'll send the DocuSign envelope for signatures and attach the dynamic Subprocessor Annex (live link in our Console).

Thanks — looking forward to getting Observa into pilot.

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Lead
Redwood Inference
